literal: Feigned anger to love [is] pleasure; to that, pleasure [is] if [one] gets to embrace having united.
translation: Feigned anger gives pleasure to love; and the pleasure of that anger is to be united in a close embrace.
modern: ஊடல் கொள்வது காமத்திற்கு இன்பம் தருகிறது; அந்த ஊடலுக்கு இன்பமாவது, மீண்டும் கூடித் தழுவப் பெறுவதாகும்.
explanation: This final couplet of the Tirukkuṟaḷ celebrates the sweet cycle of love. It states that a lover's feigned anger (ஊடுதல்) adds a unique pleasure to love (காமம்). However, that anger itself finds its ultimate pleasure (இன்பம்) only when the lovers reunite (கூடி) and embrace (முயங்க) each other. The word 'ஊடுதல்' refers to the playful sulking or tiff between lovers, which is not a real conflict but a prelude to deeper intimacy. Thus, the poet beautifully shows how temporary separation enhances the joy of union.
